title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff & regional failover load-shedding (low-latency circuit-breaker)
author: Aisha Raman
release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff behavior and prevent aggressive load-shedding for low-latency/pinned routes; improve metrics and add tests. Backported to release-2026-02.
description:
Context: During a recent regional outage we observed the SLO enforcer aggressively tripping circuit-breakers and performing load-shedding in a way that caused thrashing across regions and disproportionally impacted pinned/low-latency routes. Root cause: backoff logic lacked hysteresis and priority awareness — when a region recovered briefly it would immediately get traffic again and then be shed, causing ordering races in the regional failover path and spikes in downstream latency.

This PR: single continuous description of the changes —
- Add hysteresis to regional backoff to require a stable healthy window before clearing backoff.
- Add explicit prioritization so low-latency (pinned/SLT) routes are allowed a higher grace threshold and are rate-limited more conservatively during transient failures.
- Tighten circuit-breaker open -> half-open transition timing and add max-concurrent-try window to avoid stampedes.
- Adjust load-shedding policy to use token bucket smoothing and a small cooldown per-client to avoid repeated immediate rejections.
- Improve observability: new metrics (slo_enforcer.backoff_hysteresis_count, slo_enforcer.low_latency_bypass, slo_enforcer.cb_half_open_attempts) and dashboard panels.
- Add unit + e2e tests that simulate regional failover ordering, backoff hysteresis, and low-latency prioritization.
- Docs: update troubleshooting and runbook with mitigation steps and rollout notes.

Checklist:
- [x] Add hysteresis and priority logic to enforcer core
- [x] Add metrics and dashboard panels
- [x] Add unit + e2e tests
- [x] Run CI and fix flakes
- [x] Backport to release branch and deploy canary

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests: new coverage for backoff thresholds and priority bypass (services/slo-enforcer pkg).
- E2E: regional_failover_test.go simulates region A flaps, ensures stable failover without thrashing, asserts that pinned low-latency requests see fewer rejections.
- CI: initial run failed due to flaky test (race in mock clock) — fixed by serializing mock clock advances and re-ran. All checks passing.

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main, deploy canary to prod-c1 with 5% traffic, monitor slo_enforcer.backoff_hysteresis_count and cb_half_open_attempts for 2 hours.
- If stable, promote to 25% and then full rollout.
- Backport: cherry-picked to release-2026-02 for urgent customer impact; release branch passed smoke tests.

Backout plan:
- Revert merge or set slo-enforcer.backoff.enabled=false via feature flag (runtime-config) to restore previous behavior.

Notes:
- No user-facing API changes. This is an operational hotfix focused on runtime behavior.
- Linked support ticket SUP-9821 contains customer timeline and traffic traces.
commits: stabilize(slo-enforcer): add hysteresis to regional backoff and prioritize low-latency routes
slo-enforcer: avoid aggressive load-shedding for pinned low-latency requests (token-bucket smoothing)
circuitbreaker: add max-concurrent-try window and tighten half-open timings
tests: add unit and e2e for regional failover ordering and backoff
docs: update troubleshooting and runbook for SLO enforcer
review_comments: Daniel Kim (2026-02-20): Can you clarify how the hysteresis window size is chosen? Is it configurable per-region?

Aisha Raman (2026-02-20): Hysteresis default = 30s, chosen based on incident traces (median recovery ~18s). It's configurable via runtime-config.slo.enforcer.backoff.hysteresis_seconds and we expose per-region override in regional-config.json.
Priya Shah (2026-02-21): The priority bypass is sensible, but we need to ensure it cannot be abused to DDoS a recovering region. Add a per-client cooldown.
Aisha Raman (2026-02-21): Added client cooldown (per-client token bucket) and documented limits. See load_shed.go patch. Tests updated.
Owen Liu (2026-02-22): CI flaked on e2e: race in mock clock advance. Recommend serializing clock steps in the test harness.
Aisha Raman (2026-02-22): Fixed — serialized mock clock and added comment. Re-ran CI and all checks passed.
Daniel Kim (2026-02-23): Approved after confirming metrics and dashboards look good in staging.
